Run Commas from your AI assistant. Create checkout links, issue refunds and pull your numbers in plain English.

uncertain.access: API-key access request/approval flow is evidenced by the vendor's seller-portal JS bundle (Developer page strings) and a documented 403 'not approved by the Commas admin' error, not by a prose policy page. Whether a Commas account itself is free to open, and how long/strict approval is, could not be confirmed without logging in.
uncertain.mcp: Vendor docs (apidocs.fan, linked from the vendor dashboard; canonical commasdocs.com) document a remote 'Commas MCP Connector' with 44 tools, ChatGPT setup via https://www.fanbasis.com/mcp with OAuth login, plus a downloadable fanbasis-mcp.mcpb and an mcp-remote config pointing at https://hearty-flow-production.up.railway.app/mcp with an x-api-key header. A direct POST probe to www.fanbasis.com/mcp returned 405 (GET/HEAD only), while the railway.app endpoint returned 401 'No API key provided.' So the vendor-provided remote server is live but hosted on a railway.app subdomain; the homepage marks MCP as 'beta'.
uncertain.api_breadth: Counted roughly 35-45 public-api operations (products, checkout sessions incl. embedded, transactions/refunds, customers/charge/payment-methods, subscribers, subscriptions, discount codes, invoices, webhook subscriptions, wallet transactions); near the moderate/broad boundary, labeled moderate.

notes: fanbasis has rebranded to Commas: fanbasis.com shows 'FanBasis is now Commas!' and docs/developers/api subdomains of fanbasis.com redirect to commas.com. API base remains https://www.fanbasis.com/public-api; sandbox at https://api-sandbox.commas.net. No public docs link on the marketing site; the API docs URL (apidocs.fan) was found in the seller-portal Developer page. Keys have scopes (e.g., wallet).
